conclusion: Both explicitly approved independent repeats of the HIP 7.15 one-queue 128K layer-granularity recorder gate enter the persistent no-progress state. Repeat 1 completes warmup and measured passes 1-2, then stalls in measured prefill 3; repeat 2 completes warmup, then stalls in measured prefill 1. Together with the preceding completed layer-marker process, the fixed-stack process outcome is one completion and two failures, so per-layer system-fence marker insertion is rejected as a reliable lifecycle mitigation and no standalone heartbeat should be promoted from this evidence. Layer markers nevertheless provide the narrowest retirement evidence so far: repeat 1 last retires layer 11 and stops with layer 12's completion marker pending while the host is inside layer 13; repeat 2 last retires layer 33 and stops with layer 34's marker pending while the host is inside layer 35. In both cases, the unretired immediately preceding layer is linear-attention and the cursor lag is two checkpoint sequences. Because each layer's synchronous compact-WMMA scalar read occurs before the selected/shared MoE tail, the safe common window is the prior linear layer's post-read MoE tail or marker through the current layer's pre-read prefix. This does not identify a named kernel, and two linear-layer instances are insufficient to establish a deterministic linear-attention defect.

ordering_analysis.common_safe_window: The marker for linear layer X is enqueued but not retired; host execution reaches layer X+1 and does not return. No-progress can lie in layer X's post-D2H MoE tail or completion marker, or in layer X+1's attention/post-norm/router/scheduler prefix before or at its scalar D2H wait.
ordering_analysis.common_observation: X is linear-attention in both repeats (layers 12 and 34), while X+1 differs (linear layer 13 versus full-attention layer 35).
ordering_analysis.statistical_boundary: Thirty of forty model layers are linear-attention. Two of two instances do not establish that linear attention rather than the shared MoE tail, marker, or queue lifecycle is causal.
